title: Corporate Counsel
description: About Airwallex Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own. We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full. How you'll make impact As Corporate Counsel, you’ll support Airwallex’s growth in the UK by providing practical, business-focused legal advice on corporate, regulatory and commercial matters. You’ll work closely with Corporate Development on strategic transactions such as fundraising and M&A, partner with UK and regional leaders on new-market entry, support licence expansion, and help align Airwallex’s global policies and governance with UK and relevant EMEA requirements. You’ll also advise on marketing, referral and partnership initiatives, helping the business move quickly while managing legal and regulatory risk. Provide clear, pragmatic advice on UK and relevant EMEA legal and regulatory requirements, helping teams navigate applicable rules while enabling responsible growth. Support Corporate Development on fundraising rounds and strategic transactions, including due diligence, data rooms, corporate approvals, investment documentation, cap table changes and ongoing governance. Partner with the business, Regulatory Legal and Regulatory Compliance teams on expansion into and launches in new markets across the UK and EMEA, including regulatory mapping, entity and licensing considerations, and corporate governance requirements. Align Airwallex’s policies, procedures and corporate governance frameworks across jurisdictions, with particular focus on UK requirements. Draft, review and negotiate referral agreements, marketing and sponsorship agreements, and other commercial arrangements, ensuring risks are appropriately managed and documented. Advise on marketing, advertising and promotions, including claims, disclosures, digital campaigns, co-marketing and referral programmes, while supporting the review of customer-facing materials for legal and regulatory compliance. Coordinate and manage outside counsel on specialised matters in the UK and across EMEA, ensuring advice is high-quality, cost-effective and aligned to Airwallex’s risk appetite and business goals. Use technology and AI-enabled tools, including templates, playbooks, contract lifecycle tools and knowledge bases, to increase the speed, consistency and quality of legal work. You’ll work from our London office three days a week. What we're looking for Essentials Qualification as a solicitor or barrister in England and Wales, or an equivalent qualification in another UK jurisdiction, and in good standing with the relevant professional body. Proven experience in financial services and corporate law, preferably gained at a fast-growing technology or fintech company and/or a top-tier law firm. Demonstrated interest in financial services regulation and the fintech industry, with willingness to go deep on payments, e-money, money services and related regulatory topics in the UK and EMEA. In-depth knowledge of, or strong familiarity with, the UK legal and business environment, including how UK legislation, FCA requirements and cross-border rules impact fintech and payments businesses. Proven experience drafting and negotiating corporate and commercial agreements, with strong written and verbal communication skills that make complex issues clear to non-lawyers. Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams, including Corporate Development, Finance, Product, Compliance, Risk and Marketing, across time zones. Demonstrated capability in managing and leading outside counsel, including scoping work, controlling costs and consolidating advice into clear recommendations. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a practical, business-oriented approach and comfort operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. Preferred Experience supporting fundraising transactions, M&A or strategic investments, including due diligence and deal execution, ideally in a technology or fintech context. Prior in-house experience in a fintech, payments or broader financial services company, particularly one operating across the UK and multiple EMEA jurisdictions. Experience advising on legal issues related to marketing, advertising and promotions, including digital marketing, performance marketing, referral programmes and brand partnerships. Exposure to UK financial services regulatory frameworks, including the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, the Payment Services Regulations 2017, the Electronic Money Regulations 2011, FCA rules and guidance, and applicable financial promotions requirements. Experience partnering with Regulatory Legal, Regulatory Compliance or licensing teams on market expansion initiatives and regulatory change. Comfort using technology, AI and legal operations tools to increase the speed and quality of legal work, for example playbooks, templates, contract lifecycle tools or knowledge bases. You'll thrive here if You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken. You're comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and moving quickly anyway. You have experience at a fintech, payments company, or other highly regulated business. You say what you mean. You're direct, but you lead with respect. You connect dots across functions and hold the big picture without losing grip on the details. Learn more about your team Legal sits at the heart of the decisions that shape how Airwallex grows. This team backs the builders transforming us into a generational financial company, working alongside product, sales, and business partners every step of the way. You'll help shape a global licensing footprint most fintechs wish they had, while keeping our brand and data architecture best-in-class for customers entering the agentic economy and its regulatory demands. The hard part is helping the business move fast on product, revenue, and new-market expansion without compromising the discipline that protects the moat. It's a team for lawyers, strategists, and licensing specialists with commercial instincts, sharp judgment, and an obsession with customer-first outcomes. If you want to guide executive decisions and help build the licensing, structure, and judgment behind what comes next, this is where legal has real leverage. title: Manager/Associate Director - Project Management
description: About Relation Relation is a sector defining TechBio company developing transformational medicines, with technology at our core. Our ambition is to understand human biology in unprecedented ways, discovering therapies to treat some of life’s most devastating diseases. We leverage single-cell multi-omics from patient tissue, functional assays, and machine learning to drive disease understanding, from cause to cure. We are scaling rapidly and building a team of exceptional individuals to push the boundaries of drug discovery. You will work in highly interdisciplinary teams where biology, computation, and engineering come together to solve complex problems that have not been solved before. Our state-of-the-art wet and dry labs in the heart of London are designed to accelerate this integration and translate insight into impact. We are committed to building diverse and inclusive teams. Relation is an equal opportunities employer and does not discriminate on the basis of gender, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, gender reassignment, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, disability, or age. By joining Relation, you will help define how medicines are discovered and deliver meaningful impact for patients. The opportunity Relation is offering an outstanding opportunity for an experienced Project Manager to work in close partnership with our Programme and Project Leaders, putting you in a prime position to help shape delivery plans and drive our osteoporosis programme forward. Working across the full discovery journey, you'll help move the programme through Target ID, Hit-to-Lead, Lead Optimisation, Candidate Selection and beyond — coordinating across the multiple projects that make up the programme, our internal interdisciplinary teams, and third-party partners such as CROs, all while navigating the ambiguity of discovery-stage science with confidence. You'll operate at programme level, with visibility across every project within the osteoporosis programme, partnering with the Programme Leader and the Project Leaders who own each individual project. If this sounds like you, and you thrive in matrixed environments and want a real hand in shaping how tomorrow's medicines are discovered, come and join us in the heart of London. Day to day, you will Partner with Programme, Project Leaders and sponsors to understand the strategic objectives and delivery requirements across the programme. Orchestrate the matrix team to deliver against project objectives, motivating all team members with clear direction and communication. Work with functional leads to ensure appropriate resource allocation and to onboard supplementary resources where needed to support delivery. Proactively manage plans, budgets, risks and issues across the programme, escalating to senior management when appropriate. Support leadership in navigating high-impact, high-risk situations with clear analysis, high transparency and a spirit of partnership — even in the face of significant adversity or major obstacles. Translate scientific and strategic objectives into integrated project plans, timelines and milestones. Coordinate execution across the wet lab, ML research, data science and engineering teams, owning cross-team dependencies and prioritisation, and actively monitoring interdependencies across teams as the programme evolves. Identify and manage risks across the programme, working with team leads to mitigate blockers before they affect delivery. Coordinate joint governance bodies (steering committees, working groups, technical committees) — agendas, materials, minutes and follow-ups — and ensure decisions are documented and actioned. Communicate status clearly to internal leadership and external partners, surfacing decisions and trade-offs as they arise. Maintain project documentation, decision logs and operational hygiene to a standard that supports a multi-year, partnered effort. Coordinate resource allocation and operational support across the computational and wet lab teams where required. Identify and embed improvements to ways of working as the programme evolves. Professionally, you will have A degree in life sciences, project management, or a related field; advanced degree or equivalent industry experience welcome. Significant Programme/Project management experience in biotech, pharma, or comparable scientific R&D settings, ideally including early-stage discovery programmes (target ID through to candidate selection), sufficient to operate as the senior Project manager for a major, multi-year effort. Comfort managing a programme where scope and workstreams may evolve significantly as science matures from exploratory biology through to a defined lead series. Scientific literacy sufficient to engage credibly with discussions spanning wet lab biology, single-cell omics, and machine learning, and enough grounding in the discovery pipeline (target validation, hit-to-lead, lead optimisation) to track progress and flag risk without needing to do the science yourself. Familiarity with stage-gate or portfolio governance frameworks as applied to early discovery programmes (e.g. go/no-go criteria, TPP evolution, milestone-based progression). Experience overseeing third-party or outsourced work packages (e.g. CROs, academic collaborators, specialist service providers) — tracking deliverables, timelines, and quality against agreed scope, and escalating issues appropriately. Fluency with modern project management methodologies, artifacts and tools (e.g. MS Project, Smartsheet, Asana, Jira; Gantt, RAID logs). Strong organisational skills with a record of managing complex, interdependent works treams in matrixed environments. Comfort with the operational realities of R&D projects Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to write clearly for senior external audiences. Bonus Experience : Awareness of the discovery-to-IND pathway and its major inflection points (IND-enabling tox, CMC/formulation, DMPK, regulatory strategy) sufficient to anticipate future PM needs, even if this programme doesn't reach that stage during the role's tenure. Any exposure to pre-IND regulatory interactions or translational/preclinical handover Personally, you Are comfortable working in a matrixed environment, balancing multiple stakeholders and contributing effectively across teams. Take ownership of your work , proactively seek opportunities to contribute, and enable others to do their best work. Communicate openly and directly , give and receive feedback constructively, and handle challenging conversations with respect. Actively seek out diverse perspectives , build strong working relationships, and contribute to shared goals across teams. Embrace challenges with openness and resilience , set high standards for yourself, and strive to deliver meaningful outcomes. Working Style & Culture at Relation At Relation, we operate in a matrixed, interdisciplinary environment , where impact is driven through collaboration across scientific, technical, and operational domains. We collaborate, and you will partner with colleagues across multiple teams and projects, contributing your expertise while aligning to shared company priorities. We work together and win together! Mentor data engineers, raise the technical bar across the team, and contribute reusable patterns, reference architectures, and accelerators. Deep expertise in data modelling, warehouse/lakehouse design, and data governance. Hands-on background in SQL and Python, and fluency with at least one major cloud provider (AWS or Azure) and modern data platforms (e.g. Snowflake, Databricks). System-level judgement on how data architecture shapes AI outcomes: designing governed sources for RAG, structuring data for retrieval and orchestration, and deciding where structured outputs and tool use fit. Ability to set standards and lead engineers while remaining close to implementation. Strong stakeholder skills, including engaging senior client sponsors and explaining architectural trade-offs clearly. Strong Preference Experience architecting the data layer behind AI or analytics products in production. Informed views on the trade-offs between fine-tuning, RAG, and long-context approaches, and how each changes data architecture requirements, including context window economics and prompt caching. Familiarity with infrastructure as code, CI/CD, and observability for data platforms. Awareness of MCP and tool-orchestration concepts and their implications for composable, data-driven AI systems. Fluent use of AI-assisted development tools (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor), with a clear view of where they help and where human design judgement must lead. Security and compliance experience (e.g. ISO 27001 alignment, access control design). Consulting or advisory background, owning problems end-to-end rather than a single workstream. Nice to Have Evidence of self-directed building — side projects, internal tools, or startups. Exposure to finance data, PE/M&A, or portfolio-company environments. description: We’re on a mission to protect society from fraud and money laundering. We’ve already protected over 3 million people through life’s big transactions. Fraud and regulation are rising, costing the UK economy over £100bn every year; this makes it more difficult for businesses to protect themselves and their clients - individuals like you and me - from fraud and money laundering. Our co-founders Olly and Jack were led to this area when a friend was defrauded of £25K when buying their first property. title: Applied AI Engineer
description:
<p>At Hudson River Trading (HRT) the Applied AI team’s mission is to increase the speed and quality of work across the firm’s most consequential workflows. We build AI systems that help researchers and developers iterate faster, automate increasingly complex work, and enable autonomous exploration at a scale that would not otherwise be possible.</p> <p>We apply frontier models and agentic systems to how quantitative research, software development, and other critical work at HRT gets done. We combine cutting-edge commercial and open-source models and tools with infrastructure, research, and systems of our own.</p> <p>Our work spans the full stack required to make this successful: AI infrastructure, research engineering, post-training and reinforcement learning, agent evaluation, security and alignment, and deployment into real workflows.</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong></p> <p>Depending on your experience and interests, your work may include:</p> <ul> <li>Building scalable infrastructure for training, evaluating, and operating language models and AI agents</li> <li>Developing research environments, evaluation systems, and experimentation platforms that allow us to measure and improve agent performance</li> <li>Improving model and agent capabilities through post-training, reinforcement learning, prompting, tool design, and workflow optimization</li> <li>Designing sandboxing, policy enforcement, monitoring, and other safeguards for increasingly capable autonomous systems</li> <li>Partnering with teams across HRT to identify work AI can newly perform, develop effective solutions, and turn successful experiments into durable systems</li> <li>Evaluating new models, techniques, and products, and making informed decisions about when to build, buy, or adapt them</li> <li>Sharing technical knowledge and establishing effective practices for building and working with AI across HRT</li> </ul> <p><strong>Profile</strong></p> <ul> <li>You are an excellent engineer who can turn ambiguous problems into working systems</li> <li>You learn unfamiliar technical and business domains quickly and enjoy moving between them</li> <li>You care about advancing what AI systems can reliably accomplish</li> <li>You use rigorous measurement and experiment design to guide decisions</li> <li>You are comfortable operating across research and production engineering</li> <li>You communicate clearly and collaborate well with people from different technical backgrounds</li> <li>You are curious about the capabilities, limitations, and risks of increasingly autonomous systems</li> </ul> <p>We do not title: Senior Staff Product Engineer
description: About hyperexponential (hx) At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms. Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence. Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx. What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates. What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next. About the Engineering team At hyperexponential, engineering is at the heart of our mission to transform the insurance industry. Our engineers build and scale, enabling insurers to model complex risks and make smarter pricing decisions at speed. By combining deep technical expertise with creativity, the team pushes the boundaries of what’s possible in insurance technology. Within engineering, our product teams are cross-functional, pairing frontend and backend engineers with designers and product managers. This enables end-to-end ownership of features, with engineers contributing across design, architecture, implementation, and testing. Collaboration is a core part of how we work, ensuring that every release is both technically sound and valuable to our users. How we work We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder , and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work. We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods , usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart. We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move. Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest. A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer. The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 5 , that looks like this. What you'll be doing Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion. Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced. Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve. Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting. Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you. Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating. What you'll need to have done Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered. Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve. Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps. Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to. Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce. Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity. Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them. At Level 5 we'll also look for Set technical direction on a hard problem other engineers built on, and been judged on whether you made them faster and safer rather than on the size of your team. Held a quality bar across other people's work without becoming the gate they wait on. Led cross-cutting or decoupling work that teams adopted because it was the best path, not because it was mandated. You’re unlikely to thrive here if You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach. You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges. You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious. If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us. Compensation At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally. Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make. Benefits £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development. 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total). Company pension scheme via Penfold. Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life . Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno. Private healthcare insurance through AXA. Income protection and Life Insurance. Cycle to Work Scheme. Additional perks Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.). Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights. Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry. Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together. Interview process Initial chat with our Talent team Lead Hirer Interview Live AI Skills Assessment Values Interview with the CPTO Meet the CEO Our commitment to Diversity hxers are at the centre of everything we build. title: Senior People Partner
description: Senior People Partner Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000 Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function. THE MOMENT Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago. You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them. This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one. WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty. Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back. People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding. Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning. CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to. To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one. THE ROLE You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job: Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish. Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs. Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate. When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day. WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today. Yours The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end. Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding. Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems. Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027): Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago. Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation. Background screening in Zinc. Security clearance coordination. Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting. Our working groups and committees. Once the People Partner joins: A structured handover of the operational core. Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner. Shared Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that. Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join. Not yours Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition. The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO. Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO. THE STACK Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives. Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that. Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for. Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative. Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on. WHAT YOU’LL DO Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over. Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done. Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go. Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against. Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook. Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome. Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them. At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you. Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over. You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land. Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point. You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up. The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly. WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome. A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to. Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work. Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to. Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards. Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up. Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory. THE HONEST PART This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title. You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows. This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. It probably is for you if you want to prove you can run this function well enough, top to bottom, that a team gets built around you. If that sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, let’s talk. title: Strategic Client Manager
description: About Flock Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time. We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead. We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us! About the role Our largest fleet clients have the most vehicles, the most data and the most to gain from our connected proposition. As our Strategic Client Manager, you’ll be the main face of Flock for them, from multinationals and well-known brands to fast-growing sector leaders, and you’ll own those relationships end to end. Nearly all our business comes through brokers, so you’ll sit at the centre of the client, broker and Flock relationship, working closely with our Broker Development Managers and teams across the business. You’ll build our corporate client management approach from scratch, from account reviews and performance reporting to bringing claims, safety, underwriting and finance together for our biggest clients. You’ll report to our Head of Distribution and use AI day to day to prepare for meetings, understand accounts and improve reporting. Success means our clients stay with us and recommend us to others. What you’ll be doing Own the relationship with a portfolio of Flock’s largest fleet clients, becoming their primary point of contact and developing a strong understanding of their business. Build and run our corporate account management approach: client reviews, reporting, relationship cadence and account planning. Work closely with brokers and our Broker Development Managers to deliver a coordinated experience for every large corporate client. Bring together teams across Flock, including claims, safety, underwriting and finance, to resolve client questions and issues quickly, and build strong relationships with key stakeholders across client organisations. Identify retention risks early and create clear plans to protect our most important accounts. Help shape and improve Flock’s wider client service proposition, including account reviews, portal engagement, safety support, claims and reporting, feeding client feedback back into the business. Use AI in your day-to-day work, from account research and meeting preparation to query management, meeting summaries and client reporting. What you’ll need Strong experience within the insurance industry, with a clear understanding of the broker–client–insurer dynamic and the judgement to know where you add value, without duplicating the broker’s role, creating confusion or adding unnecessary layers for the client. Experience in a client-facing role such as insurer account or deal management, broker account management, claims relationship management or a similar position. A proven track record of managing important client relationships and delivering strong retention or customer satisfaction, with the confidence to work with senior stakeholders across clients, brokers and internal teams. Strong commercial judgement. You can identify when an account is at risk, understand what matters to the client and build a plan to retain them. Energy and ownership. You’re comfortable picking up a problem, finding the right people and driving it through to a solution. Confident using technology in your daily work, curious about how it can help you work faster and deliver a better client experience. Nice to have: experience with large, complex or multi-site corporate clients, Commercial Motor Fleet or fleet risk and safety experience, or exposure to claims or to building a client service proposition. Benefits 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖 Share Incentive Plan 📈 Workplace Pension 💰 Private Medical Insurance 🏥 (including Dental 🦷 Optical 👓 & Mental Health 💆‍♀️ support options) Various Salary Sacrifice Schemes - Holiday Purchase, Tech, Gym, Cycle to Work, Electric Vehicle, Private Medical Insurance for families 💵 Enhanced Parental Leave and Pay 🐣 £1000 toward relevant professional qualifications 🎓 £500 per annum towards learning and development 🌱 3 days paid leave for L&D purposes 🌻 We work hybrid, typically three days a week in our Central London office (fewer office days can be accommodated for longer commute times), a few minutes from Moorgate and Liverpool Street. This role is expected to be field based rather than office based, so visits to client sites, conferences and broker offices count towards office days. Making the world quantifiably safer takes more than good data. It takes a team where different perspectives are heard, and that’s a priority here. We insure fleets and drivers from every background, and we know a team built the same way makes sharper decisions and a better product for our customers. What are you waiting for?</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"201341983":0,"335551550":1,"335551620":1,"335559685":0,"335559737":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":279}"> </span></p></div><p><strong>About THG</strong></p> <p>We are THG, a global ecommerce group on a mission to be the global online leader in beauty and sports nutrition.</p> <p>Our leading retailers and brands, including LOOKFANTASTIC, Myprotein, ESPA, Perricone MD and Cult Beauty, make up our two core businesses: THG Beauty and THG Nutrition.</p> <p>From Manchester to New York, we’re powered by a team of over 2500 people who work together, lead by example, and think BIG.</p> <p>With us, you’ll go further, faster. What are you waiting for?</p> <p><strong>Location: Icon 1, WA15 0AF </strong></p> <p><strong>About the Role</strong></p> <p>We are looking for a Senior Technical Programme Manager to lead the delivery of our most important customer-facing technology programmes, reporting directly to the <strong>Chief Technology Officer</strong>.</p> <p>THG runs several high-profile ecommerce websites in nutrition and beauty, including myprotein.com and lookfantastic.com. Our websites and mobile apps are how customers find, buy and come back to our brands, and the programmes you lead will shape that experience directly.</p> <p>You will own programmes from first idea to launch, mainly across our websites and mobile apps. Examples include personalisation, loyalty and digital marketing technology, and some programmes will reach into other parts of the technology estate. The role is an even mix of programme and project management. You will run long-lived programmes that span many teams, and drive individual projects hands-on when they need it. You will work with executives to decide what gets built and in what order, and tell them plainly how delivery is going.</p> <p>You don’t need to be the architect. Our technology leaders set the technical direction and you will follow their lead. You do need to understand how large websites and apps are built well enough to plan the work, spot risks early and ask the right questions.</p> <p><strong> </strong></p> <p><strong>As a Technical Programme Manager you will:</strong></p> <p><strong>Programme Delivery</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>End-to-End Ownership:</strong> Own the delivery of large technology programmes across our websites and mobile apps, from scoping and planning through to launch and review.</li> <li><strong>Programme Planning:</strong> Build and maintain programme plans, milestones and dependency maps across several engineering and product teams.</li> <li><strong>Hands-On Project Delivery:</strong> Run individual projects directly when a programme needs it.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Prioritisation & Product Partnership</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Executive Prioritisation:</strong> Bring options, costs and trade-offs to executives and secure a clear decision on what comes first.</li> <li><strong>Backlog Management:</strong> Manage the backlog for your programmes so engineering teams always know what is next and why.</li> <li><strong>Product Collaboration:</strong> Work with product managers to turn business goals into well-defined, deliverable pieces of work.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Reporting, Risk & Vendors</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Honest Reporting:</strong> Give executives and stakeholders clear, candid updates on progress, risks and dates.</li> <li><strong>Risk & Dependency Management:</strong> Find risks, blockers and cross-team dependencies early, resolve them, and escalate when a decision is needed.</li> <li><strong>Vendor Management:</strong> Hold external vendors and delivery partners to their commitments and fit their work into our plans and releases.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Continuous Improvement</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Ways of Working:</strong> Improve how we plan, track and report on delivery across the technology organisation.</li> </ul> <p><strong>A day in the life</strong></p> <p>Your day is split between the teams doing the work and the leaders deciding what the work should be. You might start with an engineering team, checking progress against the plan and clearing a blocker, then spend time with a product manager breaking a loyalty feature into deliverable stages. In the afternoon you could review a vendor’s delivery plan for a marketing technology integration, then update programme status ahead of an executive review, where you’ll set out where things stand, what is at risk and which decisions you need. You’ll leave with clear priorities and take them back to the teams.</p> <p><strong>What skills and experience do I need for this role?</strong></p> <p><strong>Essential Requirements</strong></p> <ul> <li>Highly Skilled in technical programme or project management.</li> <li>Experience working directly with software engineering teams.</li> <li>Adept at delivering customer-facing websites or mobile apps.</li> <li>Excellent at managing programmes across several teams, including planning, dependency management and release coordination.</li> <li>Experience running prioritisation and backlog management with senior stakeholders and reporting on delivery to executives.</li> <li>Managing both external vendors or delivery partners.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Desirable Attributes</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with websites and ecommerce at large scale: high traffic, many markets, or several brands.</li> <li>Experience delivering programmes in personalisation, loyalty or digital marketing technology.</li> <li>Experience delivering native mobile apps alongside web.</li> <li>Experience in retail, particularly nutrition or beauty.</li> <li>A record of bringing clear structure to ambiguous, multi-team programmes.</li> <li>Strong written communication, with the ability to explain a complex programme to executives in plain terms.</li> </ul> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>THG is proud to be a Disability Confident Committed employer. If you are invited to interview, please let us know if there are any reasonable adjustments we can make to the recruitment process that will enable you to perform to the best of your ability.</strong></p> <p><strong>THG is committed to creating a diverse & inclusive environment and hence welcomes applications from all sections of the community.</strong></p> <p><strong>Because of the high volumes of applications our opportunities attract, it sometimes takes us time to review and consider them all. We endeavour to respond to every application we receive within 14 days. If you haven't heard from us within that time frame or should you have any specific questions about this or other applications for positions at THG please contact one of our <span class="mark75xs2u5gf" data-markjs="true" data-ogac="" data-ogab="" data-ogsc="" data-ogsb="">Talent</span> team to discuss further.</strong></p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Forward Deployed Architect
description: WHO WE ARE Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. ABOUT THE ROLE: As a Forward Deployed Architect on Notion’s Services team, you will help customers turn AI ambition into operational reality and unlock the full potential of our platform. You will partner directly with customers to design, build, and launch AI-native workflows that drive adoption, usage, and measurable business outcomes. This role sits at the center of Notion’s workflow-led GTM motion. You will partner directly with customers to understand their business goals, operating processes, technical environment, governance needs, and adoption barriers, then translate that context into scalable Notion architectures that drive measurable value. You will be hands-on across discovery, solution design, workspace architecture, workflow build, AI implementation, launch planning, adoption and handoff. You will work deeply with customers to define what Notion should own, where it should integrate with existing systems, and how Notion can become a durable operating layer for their teams. The best candidates combine strong consultative discovery, systems thinking, technical fluency, AI-native workflow design, implementation judgment and exceptional customer presence. You should be comfortable reasoning through technical tradeoffs, designing scalable solutions, and partnering closely with Forward Deployed Engineering when deeper engineering support is required. WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE: - Partner with customers on forward deployed engagements from discovery through launch, translating business goals and workflow requirements into scalable clear solution design and Notion solutions that drive durable adoption. - Design scalable Notion architectures that translate customer workflows, permission and governance needs, integrations and AI use cases into optimal workspaces that are easy to adopt, manage and scale. - Design and deploy AI-native workflows using Notion AI, custom agents, automations, Workers, Developer Platform capabilities and adjacent AI tools, partnering with Forward Deployed Engineering when advanced technical depth is needed for migrations, API constraints, security architecture or frontier implementation. - Help customers navigate change by designing adoption plans, enablement materials and launch approaches that drive sustained usage and measurable business value. - Identify repeatable patterns across customer engagements and convert them into packaged solutions, templates, reference architectures, run books, enablement assets and product feedback. - Serve as a trusted advisor to customers, simplifying complex technical requirements, making practical tradeoff recommendations and helping stakeholders align around a clear implementation path. - Partner cross-functionally with GTM, Product, Engineering, PMM, Services leadership and the partner ecosystem to scale what works beyond individual customer engagements. - Create clear implementation plans, handoff materials and success measures that align customers and internal teams on the path to value. SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: - 5+ years of experience in tech services/consulting, solutions architecture, implementation, customer engineering, or a similar customer-facing role. - Proven ability to translate ambiguous customer goals into clear workflows, implementation plans, solution architectures, and measurable success criteria. - Strong consultative discovery skills, including the ability to map current-state workflows, identify customer pain, understand operating models, surface technical constraints, and define practical future-state solutions. - Hands-on AI builder mindset, with experience using AI tools to design, prototype, automate, or improve real business workflows. - Technical fluency with APIs, integrations, data models, automation, enterprise systems, developer workflows and implementation tradeoffs. You do not need to write production code but you should be able to reason through technical constraints and troubleshoot effectively. - Strong experience delivering implementations that drive adoption, change management and long-term customer value. - Strong project and engagement management skills, including ownership of scope, timeline, deliverables, stakeholder alignment, risks, decisions, dependencies and launch readiness. - Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the ability to simplify complex technical concepts for business, technical, and executive audiences. - Strong executive presence and customer judgment, with the ability to build trust, frame tradeoffs clearly, and move ambiguous decisions forward. - Bias toward action, high learning velocity, and comfort building in fast-changing AI-native product environments. NICE TO HAVES: - Experience designing or deploying Agents, automations or AI-powered workflows with Customers. - Experience with Notion, APIs, MCPs, Workers, coding agents or developer platform workflows. - Experience developing discovery methodologies, reusable delivery assets, internal tooling, packaged services or reference architectures from the ground up. - Experience partnering with Product and Engineering teams to turn field learnings into roadmap signal, reusable architecture patterns or scalable product improvements. - Previous experience in a fast-paced, high-growth technology environment. By clicking “Submit Application”, I understand and agree that Notion and its affiliates and subsidiaries will collect and process my information in accordance with Notion’s Global Recruiting Privacy Policy https://notion.notion.site/Notion-Global-Recruiting-Privacy-Policy-fc3eb4e829354a26a2bb6fd5e289b550. https://dev.notion.so/a3ce416456924276a59de91bca740028?pvs=21 #LI-Onsite A NOTE ON AI You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement — when that’s the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on. EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & ACCOMMODATIONS We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Notion is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Consistent with applicable law, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Notion provides reasonable accommodations during the application process; if you need one, please let your recruiter know. Notion is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Notion considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Notion is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please let your recruiter know.

ABOUT THE ROLE Notion is shaping the future of Go-To-Market, and as a Solutions Consultant (SC), you’ll bring that future to life by building alongside customers and turning their biggest challenges into measurable outcomes. As a customer-facing, quota-carrying SC, you’ll bring together technical fluency and commercial ownership to grow your book of business. You’ll build pipeline with BDRs, engage key stakeholders, lead discovery, co-build workflow solutions live with customers, and guide opportunities through close. You’ll partner with BDRs, Outcomes Architects, and technical or product specialists while maintaining clear ownership of customer relationships, opportunity momentum, and next steps. If you’re a builder who loves to sell—and want to work at the intersection of AI, productivity, and enterprise—this is the role. WHAT YOU’LL ACHIEVE - Create pipeline across your book of business. Build target-account plans with BDRs and initiate outreach to priority stakeholders to generate qualified opportunities, alongside BDR-sourced pipeline. - Own opportunities from first conversation through close. Lead discovery, qualify business needs and urgency, align stakeholders, shape the solution and business case, and drive the evaluation and commercial decision. Navigate commercial sizing, proposal construction, procurement, legal, and security review to close deals with the right scope, credits, and implementation path. - Design and validate workflow solutions that deliver measurable value. Map current- and future-state workflows, co-build solutions live in Notion, and define realistic scope, success criteria, and an implementation path. Translate customer needs and validated outcomes into a clear business case, commercial recommendation, and decision path. Treat discovery as an opportunity to build and validate. - Orchestrate the right partners while maintaining ownership. Engage BDRs, Outcomes Architects, and technical or product specialists at the right moments, with clear context and asks, while owning opportunity momentum, customer communication, and next steps. - Drive customer value and commercial growth after signature. Partner with Outcomes Architects, guide the initial path to value with a clear adoption plan, on onboarding and ongoing multi-workflow adoption, and own expansion strategy and renewal planning. Stay accountable for translating credits sold into credits consumed, and surface risks or expansion opportunities as customer workflows mature. SKILLS YOU’LL NEED TO BRING - Commercial ownership and pipeline generation. You can demonstrate how you created or advanced business, influenced customer decisions, and owned measurable outcomes. title: Senior Financial Control Analyst, 9 Month Fixed Term Contract
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/personal">personal</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/business-banking">business</a> bank accounts, we offer <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/joint-account">joint accounts</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/16-17">accounts for 16-17 year olds</a>, a <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/under-16s">free kids account</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/flex">credit cards</a> in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also <a href="https://monzo.com/savings">save</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/investments">invest </a>and <a href="https://monzo.com/pensions">combine their pensions</a> with us. </p> <p>With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!</p> <p>We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️</p> <hr> <p> </p></div><p><strong>Senior Financial Control Analyst</strong></p> <p>📍London/Cardiff | 💰£56,000 - £75,000 + <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">Benefits</a></p> <p><strong>⭐ Our Financial Control Team:</strong></p> <p>Monzo is growing fast - new products, new markets and new locations. As we expand we need to make sure we can support our businesses and control our processes, so we are growing our team to meet these exciting new challenges! We are looking to introduce a Senior Financial Control Analyst on a 9 Month Fixed Term Contract. </p> <p>Our team sits within Monzo’s Finance collective and our job is getting the numbers right. We’re currently a team of seven qualified accountants, split between our Cardiff and London offices, and we ensure the ledger’s correct at every month-end. We work closely with all areas of Finance and the product teams to make that happen.</p> <p><strong>🔑 You’ll play a key role by… </strong></p> <p>We're looking for a proactive, enthusiastic and commercially-minded accountant to work on our financial accounting, and help us build a world-class finance function. This role would be well suited to a qualified accountant with 2+ years of post-qualification experience.</p> <p>We have some really exciting challenges under way like making sure we maximise our new SAP S4/HANA general ledger, expanding into the European Union, pushing forward with our automation plans, continuing to grow our customer base, growing our lending business and adding to our marketplace. You’ll work on scaling Monzo in a controlled way, while helping us optimise our financial control processes with the help of technology. You’ll report to our Financial Control Manager.</p> <p><strong>Your day-to-day:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Manage a tight process with the rest of our internal Finance team to ensure a swift month-end close process and group consolidation.</li> <li>Understand the business and our products to write insightful management commentary.</li> <li>Understand our accounting systems and make sure we are taking advantage of all features we can to minimise manual elements of reporting.</li> <li>Embrace the opportunity to improve and transform processes, driving incremental improvements through to adoption of AI.</li> <li>Learn SQL skills to run reports and propose solutions that make our processes efficient and scalable.</li> <li>Support our year end process working with external auditors and our Financial Reporting squad.</li> <li>Help review new products, assessing the accounting and implementing them in our banking platform and accounting system.</li> <li>Work with the business to assess the impact of changes in accounting standards and make proposals on accounting policy matters for new products launched.</li> <li>Help maintain the integrity of our chart of accounts and financial static data.</li> <li>Resolve miscellaneous inquiries and support the overall finance team wherever needed - from forecasting and valuations, to bank transfers, transfer pricing and tax policy research!</li> </ul> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…</strong></p> <ul> <li>You’re a qualified accountant with a few years’ post-qualification experience, ideally in financial reporting/controlling teams and working in a retail banking environment</li> <li>You have a strong understanding of technical accounting standards</li> <li>You have a great eye for detail</li> <li>You’re fascinated by the banking and regulatory landscape, and have a good understanding of key financial controls</li> <li>You’re a self-starter and enjoy tackling what needs doing, whether it’s making a bank transfer or pulling together reports for investors</li> <li>You’re comfortable translating complex information into simple words for people with diverse backgrounds</li> <li>You’re interested in using data (SQL skills would be a bonus)</li> <li>You embrace change and are motivated to improve and innovate process</li> <li>You thrive in a dynamic and constantly evolving environment</li> <li>What we’re doing at Monzo excites you!</li> </ul> <p>🙌 What’s in it for you</p> <p>💰£56,000 - £75,000. </p> <p>📍This role can be based in our London or Cardiff office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London) </p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team. </p> <p>📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.</p> <p>🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup. </p> <p>➕ Plus lots more!<a href="https://monzo.com/careers/"> Read our full list of benefits</a>.</p> <p><strong>🌈 The application journey has 4 key steps</strong></p> <ul> <li>Recruiter Screening Conversation </li> <li>Initial HM Interview </li> <li>Role Specific Interview </li> <li>Behavioural Interview </li> </ul> <p>This process should take around 3-4 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible! </p> <p>We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo.<a href="https://monzo.com/blog/the-ultimate-guide-on-using-ai-to-ace-an-interview-at-monzo"> You can read them here.</a></p> <p>#LI-TP1</p><div class="content-conclusion"><hr> <p><strong>Equal opportunities for everyone</strong></p> <p>Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/diversity-and-inclusion">blog</a>, 2026 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/our-2026-diversity-and-inclusion-report" target="_blank">Diversity and Inclusion Report</a> and 2025 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/gender-pay-gap-report-2025">Gender Pay Gap Report.</a></p> <p>We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.</p> <p>If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage 😊</p></div>

Within our People Collective, we're here to bring brilliant people together, build an inclusive culture and create an environment where everyone can do their best work. As Monzo continues to grow, our offices play an important role in bringing our people together. They're more than just places to work. They're spaces where teams connect, collaborate and experience what it means to be a Monzonaut.</p> <p>We're looking for an experienced <strong>Property & Facilities Lead</strong> to join us on a 12 month fixed term contract, covering caregiver leave. You'll lead a team of six across four office locations in London, Cardiff, Dublin and Barcelona, helping us deliver an exceptional workplace experience while managing and developing our global property portfolio.</p> <p>Reporting to the Head of Property, Culture and Engagement, you'll oversee our daily operations, lead strategic projects and collaborate with teams across Monzo to create safe, welcoming and engaging workplaces that bring people together and put the Monzonaut community first.</p> <h2><strong>🔑 You'll play a key role by...</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>🏢 Leading our global property and facilities operations</strong> – Overseeing our office locations, ensuring they're safe and compliant, while delivering a consistent and delightful workplace experience.</li> <li><strong>🚀 Managing and delivering property projects</strong> – Leading projects from planning to delivery, including office moves, refurbishments and new site launches. You'll manage timelines, budgets and internal and external stakeholders to deliver successful outcomes.</li> <li><strong>🌍 Supporting our global property strategy</strong> – Turning our longer term property ambitions into practical plans, ensuring our spaces meet the needs of our people and support Monzo's continued growth.</li> <li><strong>💪 Leading and developing a brilliant team</strong> – Managing six team members across all locations, setting clear priorities, supporting their development and building a scalable, high-performing function.</li> <li><strong>🤝 Collaborating across Monzo</strong> – Building strong relationships with Finance, Legal, TechOps and senior leadership to align priorities, influence decisions and deliver improvements.</li> <li><strong>💰 Managing budgets and suppliers</strong> – Overseeing property and facilities budgets, managing supplier relationships and ensuring we're delivering value for money across our portfolio.</li> <li><strong>🦺 Keeping our spaces safe and sustainable</strong> – Ensuring our workplaces meet health and safety requirements, managing compliance and working with the ESG team to deliver our Scope 1 and 2 environmental commitments.</li> <li><strong>✨ Continuously improving how we work</strong> – Using data and employee feedback to improve our spaces, streamline processes and build scalable ways of working. You'll also be happy to roll up your sleeves and provide hands on support when needed.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>🤩 We'd love to hear from you if...</strong></h2> <ul> <li>You have strong <strong>property and facilities management experience</strong>, ideally in a fast-paced, growing organisation with multiple office locations.</li> <li>You're an <strong>experienced project manager</strong>, confident leading complex projects end to end, managing timelines, budgets, risks and competing priorities.</li> <li>You're a <strong>confident people leader</strong>, with experience managing, coaching and developing high performing teams.</li> <li>You're <strong>commercially minded</strong>, with experience managing budgets, suppliers and contracts while balancing cost, quality and employee experience.</li> <li>You're a <strong>strong communicator and collaborator</strong>, comfortable working with senior stakeholders and building relationships across teams.</li> <li>You're <strong>proactive, organised and adaptable</strong>, able to balance day-to-day operations with strategic priorities, navigate ambiguity and make decisions independently.</li> <li>You're <strong>data-driven</strong>, and can use insights to make decisions and improve processes.</li> <li>You have a good understanding of <strong>workplace health and safety</strong>, and are confident using digital tools such as Google Workspace and Slack</li> <li>[Nice to have] You have a formal health and safety, facilities and/or project  management qualification such as IWFM 7, NVQ, NEBOSH, PRINCE 2 or APM.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Not ticking every box? At Monzo, we're committed to building a diverse and inclusive team, and we care just as much about your potential as your experience. If you're excited about this opportunity and think you could make a difference, we'd love to hear from you.</p> <h2><strong>🙌 What's in it for you</strong></h2> <p>💰 £60k - £65k + Incentive Awards</p> <p>📍 This role is based in our London office, with a minimum of three days per week in the office. You'll also travel periodically to our Cardiff, Dublin and Barcelona offices.</p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to manage your time in a way that works for you, your team and the role.</p> <p>📚 £1,000 annual learning budget to spend on books, training courses and conferences.</p> <p>🏡 We'll provide you with a MacBook and the equipment you need to work effectively.</p> <p>➕ Plus lots more!<a href="https://monzo.com/careers/"> Read our full list of benefits</a>.</p> <h2><strong>🌈 The application journey</strong></h2> <p>Our hiring process is designed to help us get to know you, your experience and how you approach real-world challenges.</p> <p>There are four stages:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Initial call</strong> – An initial conversation to learn more about you and share more about the opportunity.</li> <li><strong>Role-specific interview</strong> – A deeper conversation about your technical experience, project management and approach to leading a multi-site function.</li> <li><strong>Manager and leadership interview</strong> – An opportunity to explore your leadership style, stakeholder management and how you approach decision-making.</li> </ol> <p>We aim to complete the process in around 2–3 weeks and will be as flexible as possible to accommodate your schedule.</p> <p>We also have some guidance on using AI during your application and interview.<a href="https://monzo.com/blog/the-ultimate-guide-on-using-ai-to-ace-an-interview-at-monzo"> You can read it here.</a></p> <p>#LI-OH #LI-LONDON</p> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><hr> <p><strong>Equal opportunities for everyone</strong></p> <p>Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK.
